text: 4.2 Seriously? That's amazing! Oh, it's no big deal. I didn't even win the tournament. I lost in the semi-finals, but at least the girl who beat me went on to win the whole thing, so it wasn't too bad. So you got to the semi-finals? I can't believe it. You don't look big enough to fight, if you don't mind me saying. Well, that's why I love judo. It's nothing to do with how big you are. It's all about balance. You learn how to take advantage of your opponent's strength and size to throw them off balance. Oh right, I see. So how long have you been doing that then? Ever since I was a kid. I used to get into fights when I was at school because I was so small. The big kids used to bully me, so my dad suggested I started doing a martial art. And that was it really. You've kept very quiet about it all the time I've known you. Yeah, well, I don't like to talk about it. People might think I'm being big-headed. I don't really feel like it's connected to what I do at work. So, how often do you have to train? Well, I usually practice all the techniques for at least an hour a day, once I get home in the evening. And then, two or three times a week, I go to a special judo school to spar, you know, to practice fighting. I'm speechless, Rika. I really am. Yeah, well, there you go. And this tournament the other week, what was it exactly? Was it a big thing? Um, yeah. It was the women's national final. No! Yeah, honestly. I'm actually quite annoyed. I think I had a chance of winning it, but I hurt my back quite badly last year fighting in a competition. I didn't warm up properly before the fight, so my body wasn't really ready for it, and when I fell, I injured myself a bit. I didn't fight for a couple of months after that and it took me a while to get used to competing again. I can imagine! Yeah, but I've been doing quite a lot of yoga for the last few months and that has really helped a lot.
